title: The late hare
hook: the smallest animal walks to the lion slowly, on purpose (Masnavi 1)

segments.voice: Yesterday, tawakkul: the lion and the animals argued about trust and effort. Your line was tie your camel. What was your part, and what did you let go? Day one hundred seventy-nine.

Have you ever been late on purpose? Let the pasta water boil a little longer so the argument in the kitchen could cool. Walked around the block before going into the meeting, so you'd walk in calm instead of furious. It can feel wrong. Something says hurry. But sometimes slowing down is exactly the right move. The animals have made their deal with the lion: one of them every day, chosen by lot. The days go by. Then the lot falls on a hare, small and easy to overlook. Today, the late hare.
screen: `LATE ON PURPOSE.` → `THE LOT FALLS ON THE HARE.` → `THE LATE HARE.`

segments.voice: The hare doesn't run and hide. He says to the other animals: give me a little time. I have a plan. They're outraged. Who do you think you are? We've kept our promise to the lion all this time, and you'll ruin it. You, a hare, cleverer than all of us? The hare answers them calmly. God gives understanding to the weak as well as the strong. Rumi, through him, points to the bee: a tiny creature, and yet, the Quran says, God inspired it to build and make honey. Size isn't wisdom. So they let him go. And he walks. Slowly. He takes his time on the road. He stops. He thinks. He lingers. Meanwhile, the lion waits. Hour after hour, no meal. The lion paces, roars, claws the ground. He says to himself: I knew it. They cheated me. I'll never trust them again. Rumi spends lines on that rage: how anger blinds, and how being sure of yourself can make you easy to fool. By the time the little hare finally strolls up, the lion is almost out of his mind. Why are you late? he roars. And the hare bows and begins to tell a story. We'll hear it tomorrow. For today, notice the strategy. The hare can't outfight the lion. He can't outrun him forever. But he can choose his pace, and the lion can't. He slows down on purpose, and the lion's own hurry becomes the lion's weakness. Your line: the late hare.
screen: `GIVE ME TIME: I HAVE A PLAN.` · `THE BEE: SMALL, AND INSPIRED.` · `THE HARE WALKS SLOWLY.` · `THE LION'S RAGE BLINDS HIM.` · then, large: `THE LATE HARE.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: slow one thing down on purpose. Settle, and breathe. Now take the next thing you do, standing up, reaching for your phone, even the next breath, and do it at half speed. Notice the urge to hurry. It's strong. Let it be there, and don't obey it. Breathe out slowly, slower than you'd like. Feel what it's like to set your own pace. The bell holds the time.
Masnavi, Rumi's book of stories: the hare chosen for the lion walks to him slowly, on purpose, while the lion's rage grows. Today's word.
Your line: he slows down on purpose. Today, before one tense moment, a reply, a call, a meeting, take an extra minute on purpose and walk in calm. Day one hundred seventy-nine.

screen: `DAY 179 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: THE LION IN THE WELL.`

howItsDone: The lion and the hare is a Masnavi story with older roots in the animal fables of Kalila and Dimna, which descend from the Indian Panchatantra; Rumi retells it with his own long reflections.

original.note: Persian: hare, rabbit. the smallest hero in the Masnavi.

trapdoor: what you thought: the tortoise and the hare, again.
what it means: the weakest animal wins by choosing his pace, while the strongest is undone by his own rage.
what a scholar hears: the tale comes into Persian through Kalila and Dimna, from the Panchatantra; Rumi slows it with long reflections on anger, fate and inspiration.

notes: Masnavi paraphrased: the lot falling on the hare, the animals' objection, the hare's answer that God gives wisdom to the weak with the example of the bee, the slow walk, the lion's rage. Confirm the bee example is in this passage (Rumi cites Quran 16:68).
Kalila and Dimna / Panchatantra as the older source of the lion-and-hare fable: confirm.
Rumi's reflections on the lion's anger summarized loosely; confirm.
